method: Weight is estimated with the standard length-girth field formula W = L * G^2 / K, where L is the length from snout to tail fork with the tail pinched, G is the girth around the widest part of the body with the fins folded, both measured in inches, and K is a shape factor of 800 by default; the result is reported in pounds, kilograms at 0.45359237 kg per pound, and ounces at 16 per pound. The same fish is recomputed at shape factors of 700, 800, 900 and 1000 to show how much body shape moves the estimate, and the girth-to-length ratio is reported as a condition indicator. Length accepts 1-100 in (2.5-254 cm) and girth 0.5-100 in (1.3-254 cm), with centimetre input converted exactly at 2.54 cm per inch; girth may not exceed the length, and the shape factor is limited to 400-2000. Species, condition factor, spawn state, stomach contents, girth measurement error and the divergence of very large or very slender fish from the formula are not modelled, so the result is an estimate that can be off by roughly a tenth either way and is no substitute for a scale. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: R. O. Anderson and R. M. Neumann, Length, Weight, and Associated Structural Indices, in Fisheries Techniques, 2nd ed., American Fisheries Society, 1996 (length-weight relations)
Standard length-girth field formula W (lb) = length (in) x girth (in)^2 / 800, as published in freshwater angling field guides
